_comment: What this board's analog path IS, measured against an instrument
that is not the ADC. Moved here from tests/baseline.json on
2026-08-27, unchanged: the numbers were right and the home was
wrong. host/receive.py, gui/stream.py, gui/awg.py and
tools/dso_metrics.py were all reaching into a test fixture for
them, so every volt the front end drew came out of a file whose
job is regression tolerances.
The split: this file is what the hardware is; baseline.json is
what its behaviour is expected to be. Read it through
host/calibration.py, which is the only reader - one home for the
number and one implementation of finding it.
The DAC's output span, measured with the SCOPE on the pin, not
through the ADC. span_lo/span_hi used to be ADC-derived - a mean
code times 3300/4095 - which folds the ADC's own offset into the
DAC's span and reads about 32 mV low at the bottom. The two agree
once that offset is accounted for, which is the check that
settled it; before the scope there was no third party to ask.
tools/dso_metrics.py transfer, 8 agreeing points of 10, repeats
spread 1.2-8.1 mV, worst deviation from the fit 4.4 codes.
The DAC->ADC loop is RATIOMETRIC: the DAC's reference is ADVREF,
the ADC's reference (datasheet Table 46-39's note, recorded in
docs/HANDOFF.md). One reference, so the loop's code-to-code ratio
is immune to what the 3.3 V rail actually is - and, by the same
token, blind to it. The board cannot measure its own reference.
The scope supplies exactly that missing scale, and two
independent routes agree to 0.1 mV: the loop slope against the
scope's DAC span, and the ADC's codes-per-millivolt directly.
Both give ADVREF = 3270 mV, not the 3300 that host/ and tests/
have assumed.
So the +0.91% first reported as an ADC gain error is very likely
not the ADC's at all - it is the assumed reference being high. A
ratiometric loop cannot separate those two; only an external
instrument can, which is the whole argument for having one.
What is NOT claimed: absolute accuracy. This is ADVREF as a
DS1102E with an asserted probe ratio sees it. A 6.5-digit meter
would move it and would be believed over this.
_offset_note: A separate offset term is deliberately NOT recorded. The DAC only
spans 578-2771 mV, so an offset at code 0 is extrapolated outside
the data and is strongly correlated with the slope: the -47 codes
the first fit reported is mostly a 0.9% slope error walked back
from mid-scale. Over the measured range a single scale factor
reconciles the two instruments to about 4 codes.
